The method

Four stages. One outcome.

01 / LEARN

Structured, not scattered

Small batches, certified trainers, and a curriculum sequenced the way the work is actually done — not the way a menu is organised.

02 / BUILD

Projects, not exercises

You build real deliverables: a coordinated model, a corridor design, a manufacturable assembly, a printed prototype. They become your portfolio.

03 / EXPERIENCE

Beyond the classroom

Industry visits, technical competitions, workshops, guest sessions from practising engineers, and a lab you can use.

04 / CAREER READY

Prepared, not just certified

Portfolio review, CV and profile work, mock interviews, certification preparation, and introductions through our Industry Recruitment Panel.

    Home / Careers

    What happens after
    the certificate.

    A certificate on its own does not get anybody hired. A portfolio, a straight answer in a technical interview, and somebody willing to make an introduction — that is what moves people from trained to employed. This is what we do about it.

    Placement support

    Described honestly.

    A lot of training providers advertise 100% placement. We do not, because it is not a claim anyone can honestly stand behind.

    What we do

    Portfolio development.
    You finish with real project work, presented properly. For technical roles, the portfolio does more work than the CV.
    CV and profile.
    We rewrite your CV against the roles you are targeting and get your LinkedIn profile into a state where recruiters find it.
    Mock interviews.
    Technical questioning by a trainer who has worked in the field, followed by honest feedback about what you got wrong.
    Industry Recruitment Panel.
    Introductions to employers in our network who are actively hiring.
    Internship guidance.
    Where a full role is not immediately available, we help you find project-based work that builds experience.

    What we cannot do

    We cannot guarantee you a job. Hiring depends on your background, how much effort you put into your portfolio, how you interview, and the state of the market that quarter.

    What we can guarantee is that you will not walk into an interview unprepared.

    Home / Careers / First Job Pakka

    A CADD Centre national initiative

    First Job Pakka.
    In 80 hours.

    The first job is the hardest one to get. First Job Pakka is CADD Centre's training-and-placement initiative, built around a simple idea: eighty focused hours on the right skills, aimed squarely at making you employable rather than merely certified.

    Find my career path
    What makes it different

    Three things, done deliberately.

    This is not a repackaged software course. The structure is built backwards from what employers actually screen for.

    Core competence

    A holistic approach covering engineering design and development alongside project management. Expert training on the CAD and CAE tools employers use, taught with the engineering concepts behind them — so you learn how the tools are used in real engineering work, not just which buttons produce which result.

    Hands-on

    Practical application in the lab, with the theory taught alongside rather than in front. You get time and space to think through each action, and a trainer who can give real-time feedback while you are still making the mistake — which is when feedback is worth something.

    Programming skills for engineers

    Whatever branch of engineering you are in, computational skill is now a baseline expectation. AI, IoT and robotics are creating engineering jobs that assume some knowledge of programming and algorithms. This is the part most CAD training leaves out entirely.

    Why this matters here

    The programming component is the differentiator

    Every CAD institute in Gurugram teaches the same software. Very few of them teach engineers to think computationally alongside it.

    That combination — a design tool plus the ability to automate and reason about it — is what separates an engineer who can operate software from one who can improve how their team works. It is also the capability that ages best as tooling changes.

    First Job Pakka also includes exposure to job fairs and pre-placement assessment as part of the national programme.

    wireframe
    Being precise about what this is. First Job Pakka is a training-and-placement initiative, not a job guarantee — and we will not describe it as one. Ask an advisor which programmes qualify, what the eligibility is, and exactly what placement support is included. You will get a straight answer.

    Ask us what it means for you.

    Bring your background and your timeline. We will tell you honestly whether this route fits.

    Home / Apply as Mentor

    Teach what you
    actually practise.

    Every trainer here worked in the field before they taught it, and most still do. If you have built the thing you would be teaching — coordinated a model, run a corridor design, taken a part to manufacture, held a programme to schedule — we would like to hear from you.

    Apply now
    Who we look for

    Practitioners, not presenters

    Industry experience first

    Time spent doing the work on real projects, not only time spent teaching it. That is what learners can tell the difference between.

    Depth in one discipline

    Strong in one area — BIM, civil, structural, mechanical, MEP, visualisation or project planning — beats a shallow pass across all of them.

    Willing to be questioned

    Our sessions are hands-on and learners interrupt. The trainers who do well here enjoy that rather than tolerate it.

    What it involves

    • Teaching to a set curriculum, with room to bring your own project examples
    • Reviewing learner work and giving usable feedback, not just marks
    • Mock interviews and portfolio reviews as learners approach placement
    • Keeping your own material current as the software moves

    How it fits around a job

    Most of our trainers teach alongside practice. Batches run on weekday evenings and at weekends as well as in the day, so tell us honestly what you can commit to — we would rather build a schedule around you than have you drop a batch halfway through.

    Terms are discussed individually and depend on discipline, experience and how much you want to take on.

    Application

    Apply as a mentor

    Tell us what you have built and what you could teach. If there is a fit, someone from the centre will call you.

    We will call or message on WhatsApp

    We read every application. If your discipline is not one we are running right now we will say so rather than leave you waiting.

    Home / About

    CADD Centre Gurugram,
    Sector 14.

    We run industry-focused programmes in CAD, BIM, product design, structural engineering, project management and AI-assisted engineering workflows. We are an Authorised Training Centre of CADD Centre Training Services, and we are operated by Vara Global Tech.

    The local part matters more than the national part

    What the franchise means in practice is that we carry the curriculum, certification and standards of a national training network, and we run them locally — with our own trainers, our own labs, our own equipment, and our own relationships with employers in the NCR.

    A curriculum is a document. What actually determines whether you come out employable is who teaches you, how much you build, and who is willing to introduce you to a hiring manager. Those things happen in a room in Sector 14, not on a network map.

    What we do differently

    We organise around careers, not software.
    You should not need to know whether you want Revit Structure or Civil 3D before you can talk to us.
    We publish real work.
    Everything in Student Work was made here, by learners.
    We name our trainers.
    You know who will teach you, and you can meet them before you pay.
    We are honest about placement.
    We do not advertise guarantees we cannot keep.
    Who teaches you

    Practitioners, not presenters.

    Every trainer here worked in the field before they taught it. You will know your trainer's name, their background and their experience before you enrol — and you can meet them in a free demo class before you pay anything.

    Meet them before you enrol. We would rather you met your trainer in person than read a paragraph about them. Book a free demo class and sit in on the session you would actually be joining.

    Come and see it. That invitation is not a formality — the equipment is the argument.

    Workstations & labs

    Licensed software on machines specified for the work — modelling, rendering and analysis have very different demands.

    The 3D printing lab

    Where a CAD model becomes a physical part you can hold. Open to learners across the mechanical and product design paths.

    Classrooms & review space

    Small batches, so a trainer can look over your shoulder while you are still making the mistake.

    The network behind this centre

    CADD Centre Training Services was founded in 1988 and has grown into one of Asia's largest CAD training networks.

    CADD Centre has long been at the forefront of design engineering, transforming lives through future-ready learning. From being a trusted technical training institute to becoming a hub for next-generation skill development, CADD Centre has continuously evolved to meet the demands of a dynamic world.

    Home / Career paths / BIM & Digital Construction

    Build a career in
    BIM & Digital Construction.

    BIM is not a piece of software. It is how large projects are now run — a single coordinated model that architects, structural engineers and MEP teams all work against, so clashes are found on a screen rather than on site. Firms across the NCR, the Gulf and the UK are hiring for it faster than people are training for it.

    BIM Modeller · Revit Technician · BIM Engineer · BIM Coordinator · Documentation Lead

    Talk to a career advisor Not sure? Try the finder
    The work

    What this work actually involves

    A BIM modeller builds and maintains the model to a standard the whole project team can rely on. A coordinator sits a level above: running clash detection between disciplines, chairing coordination reviews, managing model federation, and keeping the information structure consistent as the project changes.

    It is precise, collaborative work. You will spend as much time on naming conventions, worksets and information standards as on geometry, because the value of BIM is the data, not the picture.

    Skills roadmap

    The sequence that gets you there

    AutoCAD fundamentals→Revit Architecture→Revit Structure / MEP→Navisworks clash detection→Model federation→ISO 19650 concepts→Live coordination project
    Roles

    Roles this leads to

    RoleWhat you would do
    BIM ModellerBuild and maintain discipline models to project standards
    Revit TechnicianProduce construction documentation from the model
    BIM EngineerOwn a discipline model and its data integrity
    BIM CoordinatorRun clash detection and cross-discipline coordination
    Documentation LeadManage drawing production and issue control

    Home / Career paths / Civil & Infrastructure Design

    Build a career in
    Civil & Infrastructure Design.

    Infrastructure work is unforgiving about accuracy. A corridor design carries earthwork quantities that turn into real money, and a surface model that is wrong is wrong all the way to site.

    Civil Design Engineer · Highway Design Engineer · Quantity Engineer · Site Design Coordinator

    Talk to a career advisor Not sure? Try the finder
    The work

    What this work actually involves

    This path moves you from 2D drafting into 3D corridor modelling and quantity extraction — the skills that infrastructure consultancies and contractors actively recruit for. You will work with survey data, build surfaces, set out alignments and profiles, and produce the quantities a contractor prices from.

    If you like work where the answer is either right or demonstrably wrong, this suits you.

    Skills roadmap

    AutoCAD Civil→Surfaces & terrain→Alignments & profiles→Corridor modelling→Quantity take-off→Civil 3D live project

    Mechanical & Product Design.

    Product design is where a drawing has to survive contact with a machine shop. A model that looks right and cannot be made is a failed design.

    Design Engineer · Product Design Engineer · CAD Engineer · Detailing Engineer

    Revit Architecture course in Gurgaon

    Don't just learn Revit Architecture.
    Learn how buildings are designed in BIM.

    ★★★★★  4.9 on Google · 207 reviews

    Download syllabus

    Department · BIM & Digital Construction  /  9 modules

    Duration

    Approx. 60 hours

    Format

    Classroom + online

    Projects

    Live project

    Certification

    Outcome Curriculum Certification Eligibility Careers Batches FAQs
    Outcome

    What this qualifies you to do

    BIM Modeller
    Revit Technician
    Architectural Designer
    Documentation Assistant

    Part of the BIM & Digital Construction career path.

    Deliverable

    What you will have built

    A complete multi-storey building model — levels, grids, walls, floors, roofs, curtain systems, stairs and custom families — taken through to a coordinated drawing set with schedules and quantities extracted from the model itself.

    This becomes a substantial piece in your portfolio, and it is what you will be asked about in an interview.

    Curriculum

    What you will learn

    The sequence follows how the work is actually done, not how the software's menus are organised.

    • Templates, levels and grids
    • The BIM way of thinking about a building
    • Project browser and view organisation
    • Walls, compound structures and layers
    • Floors and floor systems
    • Roofs, ceilings and voids
    • Doors and windows
    • Joinery and fixed furniture
    • Component placement and constraints
    • Curtain walls, grids and mullions
    • Stairs and ramps
    • Railings and balustrades
    • Topography and toposurfaces
    • Site components and grading
    • Building pads
    • Family editor fundamentals

    Design Engineer
    Product Design Engineer
    CAD Engineer

    Part of the Mechanical & Product Design career path.

    Deliverable

    What you will have built

    A complete mechanical assembly — modelled as individual parts, assembled with correct mates, checked for interference, dimensioned and toleranced to a manufacturable standard, and issued as a full drawing set. Where the part suits it, you will 3D print a component.

    This becomes a substantial piece in your portfolio, and it is what you will be asked about in an interview.

    Curriculum

    What you will learn

    The sequence follows how the work is actually done, not how the software's menus are organised.

    • Sketch entities and relations
    • Fully defined sketches
    • Design intent
    • Extrude, revolve, sweep, loft
    • Fillets, chamfers and draft
    • Patterns and mirrors
    • Configurations and design tables
    • Multibody techniques
    • Surfacing fundamentals
    • Mates and degrees of freedom
    • Subassemblies
    • Interference and collision detection
    • Views, sections and details
    • Dimensioning standards
    • Bill of materials
    • GD&T fundamentals
    • Datums and feature control frames
    • Fit and function
    • Sheet metal features and flat patterns
    • Weldment structures
    • Manufacturing considerations
    • Full assembly from brief to drawing set
    • Prototype where suitable
    • Design review
    SolidWorks · GD&TMechanicalProfessional
    Careers

    Where this leads

    The manufacturing belt around Gurugram, Manesar and Bhiwadi runs on exactly this skill set. Automotive component suppliers, machine builders and product firms all need engineers who can model a part and then produce a drawing a shop floor can work from. The drawing matters as much as the model, which is why GD&T sits inside this programme rather than beside it.

    AutoCAD Basic Drawing: A Complete Beginner's Guide

    A practical starting guide to AutoCAD drafting — setup, the commands that matter, and the habits that make later work easier.

    wireframe

    Start with the setup, not the commands

    Most beginners open AutoCAD and start drawing lines. That works for about twenty minutes, and then the drawing becomes unmanageable. Units, limits, layers and a template are boring for ten minutes and save hours afterwards.

    The commands that carry most of the work

    A small set of commands does most real drafting: LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, OFFSET, TRIM, EXTEND, FILLET, COPY, MOVE, MIRROR and ARRAY. Learn these to the point of not thinking about them before adding anything else.

    Precision is not optional

    Drawing by eye is the single most common beginner habit and the hardest to unlearn. Object snaps, polar tracking and typed coordinates exist so that geometry is exact. A drawing that looks right and measures wrong is worse than no drawing.

    Layers are how drawings stay readable

    Layers separate what a drawing is made of. Set them up early with sensible names, colours and linetypes. When somebody else opens your file — and they will — layers are what makes it navigable.

    Annotation and output

    A drawing communicates or it fails. Dimension styles, text styles, layouts, viewports and plot scales are the part that turns geometry into something a workshop or a site can use.

    Where this leaves you

    If you are learning AutoCAD to get work rather than as a hobby, the drafting standard matters more than the software speed. Employers look at whether your drawing is readable, correctly layered and correctly annotated.

    Learning this properly? Our AutoCAD programmes cover this material with live projects and a portfolio deliverable at the end.
    See AutoCAD programmes Find my career path

    Home / News / AutoCAD

    Master AutoCAD 2D Mechanical Drawing

    How mechanical parts are actually drafted in 2D — projection, sections, tolerancing and the drawing conventions a shop floor expects.

    wireframe

    Orthographic projection is the foundation

    Mechanical drawing is a language, and projection is its grammar. First-angle and third-angle projection describe the same part differently, and getting the convention wrong makes a drawing actively dangerous rather than merely unclear.

    Sections and auxiliary views

    Internal features cannot be described with hidden lines alone once a part gets complex. Full sections, half sections, offset and revolved sections each exist for a reason, and picking the right one is a design decision.

    Dimensioning with intent

    Every dimension on a drawing is an instruction to somebody making the part. Dimension from datums that reflect how the part functions and how it will be held during machining, not from whichever edge is convenient.

    Tolerances and fits

    A dimension without a tolerance is an unanswered question. Understanding clearance, transition and interference fits — and where each is appropriate — is what makes a drawing manufacturable rather than aspirational.

    Title blocks, BOM and standards

    Revision control, part numbers, material specification and surface finish are not administrative overhead. They are how a drawing survives contact with a real supply chain.

    Where this leaves you

    2D mechanical drafting is often described as obsolete. It is not — in most Indian manufacturing and fabrication firms, the issued drawing is still 2D, even when the design was modelled in 3D. It remains directly employable.

    Learning this properly? Our AutoCAD programmes cover this material with live projects and a portfolio deliverable at the end.
